hook.title: Ek baar likho, har jagah use karo
hook.md:
Hospital pharmacy ka ek app kai jagah shareer ke wazan se dose nikaalta hai: prescription screen par, label par, stock report mein. Agar formula das jagah copy ho aur kisi ek copy mein galti ho, to patient ko galat dose mil sakta hai.

Ilaaj hai formula ko **ek baar** likhna, use ek **naam** dena, aur har jagah wahi naam use karna. Code ka yeh naam wala, dobara use hone wala hissa **function** hai. Lesson 1.1 se aap functions use kar rahe hain: `print()`, `len()` aur `input()`. Aaj aap apna function likhenge.

learn: **def** se function **define** karna, aur use **call** karna
**Parameters** se function alag-alag values ke saath kaise kaam karta hai
**return** nateeja wapas kaise bhejta hai, aur yeh print jaisa kyon nahi
**Default values** aur **local variables** kaise kaam karte hain

explanation.heading: Aapka pehla function
explanation.md:
Function ko keyword **def**, ek naam, brackets aur colon se **define** karte hain. Neeche ki indent ki hui lines uski **body** hain:

```python
def label():
    print("Keep out of reach of children")
    print("Store below 25 C")

label()
label()
```

Yeh print karta hai:

```
Keep out of reach of children
Store below 25 C
Keep out of reach of children
Store below 25 C
```

Function define karne se woh **chalta nahi**. Python bas use yaad rakh leta hai. Body tab chalti hai jab aap function ka naam brackets ke saath likhkar use **call** karte hain: `label()`.

callout.title: Function
callout.md: Code ka naam wala block jo ek kaam karta hai. def se use ek baar define karte hain, aur jab chahein uska naam brackets ke saath likhkar chalaate hain.

explanation.heading: Parameters: function ko jaankaari dena
explanation.md:
Jab aap function ko values de sakein, to woh kahin zyada kaam ka ho jaata hai. `def` ke brackets ke andar ke naam **parameters** hain:

```python
def dose_label(drug, mg):
    print(f"{drug}: {mg} mg")

dose_label("Paracetamol", 500)
dose_label("Amoxicillin", 250)
```

Yeh print karta hai:

```
Paracetamol: 500 mg
Amoxicillin: 250 mg
```

Call mein aap jo values dete hain, jaise `"Paracetamol"` aur `500`, woh **arguments** hain. Yeh parameters se **kram mein** milte hain: pehla argument `drug` mein, doosra `mg` mein.

explanation.heading: return: nateeja wapas bhejna
explanation.md:
`print()` value ko sirf screen par dikhaata hai. Function ke nateeje ko program mein aage **use** karne ke liye function ko use **return** karna hoga:

```python
def child_dose(weight, mg_per_kg):
    return weight * mg_per_kg

dose = child_dose(20, 15)
print("Dose:", dose, "mg")
print("Two doses:", child_dose(20, 15) * 2, "mg")
```

Yeh print karta hai:

```
Dose: 300 mg
Two doses: 600 mg
```

`return` value ko us jagah wapas deta hai jahaan function call hua tha, taaki aap use store karein, print karein, ya usse hisaab lagaayein. Yeh function ko khatam bhi karta hai: `return` ke baad ki lines kabhi nahi chalti.

callout.title: return nahi, to None
callout.md: Bina return ka function None deta hai, jo Python mein "kuch nahi" ka shabd hai. Agar function mein return ki jagah print karein, to dose = child_dose(20, 15) mein None store hota hai.

explanation.heading: Default values aur naam wale arguments
explanation.md:
Parameter ki ek **default value** ho sakti hai, jo call mein na di jaaye to use hoti hai. Call mein arguments ko naam se bhi de sakte hain, tab unka kram matter nahi karta:

```python
def dose_label(drug, amount, unit="mg"):
    print(f"{drug}: {amount} {unit}")

dose_label("Paracetamol", 500)
dose_label("Insulin", 10, "units")
dose_label(unit="ml", drug="Cough syrup", amount=5)
```

Yeh print karta hai:

```
Paracetamol: 500 mg
Insulin: 10 units
Cough syrup: 5 ml
```

Default wale parameters, bina default walon ke **baad** aane chahiye.

explanation.heading: Function ke andar ke variables andar hi rehte hain
explanation.md:
Function ke andar bana variable **local** hota hai: woh sirf function chalne tak rehta hai.

```python
def total_tablets(per_day, days):
    total = per_day * days
    return total

print(total_tablets(2, 5))
```

Yeh `10` print karta hai. Par function ke baad `print(total)` likhein to `NameError: name 'total' is not defined` aayega, kyonki function khatam hote hi `total` gaayab ho gaya. Bahar value use karni ho to use **return** kijiye.

Yeh achchhi baat hai: har function ke apne variables hote hain, isliye functions galti se ek-doosre ki values nahi badal sakte.

callout.title: Functions kyon likhein?
callout.md: Ek baar likho, kai baar use karo. Galti ek jagah theek karo. Kisi step ko saaf naam do, jaise mg_to_g. Aur har hisse ko alag se test karo.

walkthrough.intro: Yeh program milligrams ko grams mein badalne wala function define karta hai, phir use do baar call karta hai.

keyTerms.meaning: mg_to_g naam ka function define karo, ek parameter ke saath.
Ek parameter: har call mein di gayi value leta hai.
Nateeja call karne wale ko wapas bhejo.
Function ko argument 500 ke saath call karo.

steps.say: Yeh program conversion ko ek baar, function ke roop mein likhta hai, aur use do baar use karta hai.
Comment batata hai ki function kya karta hai.
def, m g to g naam ka function banaata hai, jiska ek parameter hai, m g. Python use yaad rakhta hai, par body abhi nahi chalaata.
Yahaan function ko paanch sau ke saath call kiya gaya. Python function mein koodta hai, aur parameter m g ko paanch sau milta hai.
Andar, grams hai paanch sau bhaag ek hazaar: zero dashamlav paanch.
return, zero dashamlav paanch ko us line par wapas bhejta hai jisne function call kiya.
Line chhah par wapas, call ki jagah uska nateeja aa jaata hai, aur print use dikhaata hai.
Wahi function phir call hota hai, do hazaar paanch sau ke saath. Is baar woh do dashamlav paanch return karta hai.

errors.intro: Yeh do errors function ko call karne ke tareeke se aati hain.

examples.title: Define karne se pehle function call karna
examples.md: Python upar se neeche chalta hai, isliye line 1 par usne abhi `def` dekha hi nahi. Function definitions upar rakhiye, call karne se pehle.

examples.title: Ek argument chhod dena
examples.md: Function ke do parameters hain, par call sirf ek value deta hai. Dono dijiye: `child_dose(20, 15)`, ya parameter ko default value dijiye.

mistakes.mistake: Call karte samay brackets bhool jaana, jaise `label()` ki jagah `label`
mistakes.see: Koi error nahi, par kuch nahi hota

mistakes.mistake: Function mein return ki jagah print karna, phir nateeje se hisaab lagaana
mistakes.see: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'NoneType' and 'int'
mistakes.fix: Value wapas bhejne ke liye `return` use kijiye; zaroorat ho to bahar print kijiye.

mistakes.mistake: `return` ke baad lines likhna aur ummeed karna ki woh chalengi
mistakes.see: Koi error nahi, par woh lines kabhi nahi chalti
mistakes.fix: Function ko jo kuch karna hai, woh sab `return` se pehle rakhiye.

mistakes.mistake: Arguments galat kram mein dena, jaise `dose_label(500, "Paracetamol")`
mistakes.see: Koi error nahi, par label par "500: Paracetamol mg" aata hai
mistakes.fix: Parameters ka kram milaaiye, ya naam dijiye: `dose_label(drug="Paracetamol", mg=500)`.

quiz.q: Python mein kaun-sa keyword function define karta hai?
quiz.why: Functions def, naam, brackets aur colon se define hote hain.

quiz.q:
def double(x):
    return x * 2

print(double(4))

Yeh kya print karta hai?
return statement na ho to function kya wapas deta hai?
quiz.why: return ke bina Python None wapas deta hai.

quiz.q: def child_dose(weight, mg_per_kg): mein weight kya hai?
quiz.why: def ke brackets ke naam parameters hain; call mein di gayi values arguments hain.

quiz.q:
def greet(name="Patient"):
    print("Hello", name)

greet()

Yeh kya print karta hai?
quiz.why: Koi argument nahi diya gaya, isliye default value "Patient" use hoti hai.

quiz.q: Function ke andar return ke baad likhi lines ka kya hota hai?
quiz.why: return function ko turant khatam kar deta hai.

exam.note: Practice ke liye important questions. University ke asli questions alag ho sakte hain.

summary: **Function** code ka naam wala block hai. **def** use define karta hai; woh tabhi chalta hai jab aap use brackets ke saath **call** karein, jaise `label()`.
**Parameters** `def` line ke naam hain; **arguments** call mein di gayi values hain, jo kram se ya naam se milti hain.
**return** nateeja call karne wale ko wapas bhejta hai aur function khatam karta hai; bina `return` ka function **None** deta hai.
Parameter ki **default value** ho sakti hai, jo call mein na di jaaye to use hoti hai.
Function ke andar bane variables **local** hote hain: function khatam hote hi gaayab, isliye jo chahiye use return kijiye.

steps.say: def lines bas Python ko ek naya shabd sikhaati hain, m g to g. Abhi kuch nahi chalta.
Aakhri line function ko paanch sau ke saath call karti hai. Python function mein koodta hai, aur parameter m g ko paanch sau milta hai.
Body grams nikaalti hai: zero dashamlav paanch.
return, zero dashamlav paanch ko wahaan wapas le jaata hai jahaan function call hua tha.
Call, zero dashamlav paanch ban jaata hai, aur print use dikhaata hai.

glossary.meaning: Naya function define karne wala keyword: def name(parameters): aur uske neeche indent ki hui body.
Function ka naam brackets ke saath likhkar use chalaana, jaise label() ya mg_to_g(500).
def ke brackets ke andar ka naam. Har baar function call hone par ise ek value milti hai.
Call mein function ko di gayi asli value, jaise mg_to_g(500) mein 500.
Nateeja wahaan wapas bhejta hai jahaan function call hua tha, aur function khatam karta hai.
Python mein "kuch nahi" ki value. Bina return ka function None wapas deta hai.
def mein parameter ko di gayi value, jaise unit="mg". Call mein woh argument na ho to yahi use hoti hai.
Function ke andar bana variable. Yeh sirf function chalne tak rehta hai.
